chunks: And Ibn Abi ʿUmayr narrated from some of his companions, from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام: concerning

A Muslim man who was in the land of shirk, and the Muslims killed him; then the Imam came to know of him afterward, so he said: “In his place, a believing slave is to be freed, and that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”
“And if he was from a people hostile to you, while he was a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave.”

The Book of Blood-Money is complete, and it is the end of the book. And praise belongs to Allah, at the beginning and the end. Completed, and praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds, what we intended of the commentary upon the tenth part—according to our division—of the Book Tahdhib al-Ahkam; and with it the book is complete. And our final call is that praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds, who guided us to this and granted us success for the completion. That was in the afternoon of Sunday, the sixteenth of the exalted month of Shaʿban, one thousand three hundred and eighty of the Prophetic Hijrah—upon his migration be thousands of praises and salutations. And I am the least, Hasan al-Mousawi al-Khursan.

key_terms.أَرْضِ ٱلشِّرْكِ: the territory of shirk, meaning a land identified with non-Muslim hostile rule
key_terms.رَقَبَةٌ مُؤْمِنَةٌ: a believing slave, whose emancipation serves as expiation
key_terms.عَدُوٍّ: an enemy people or hostile group
key_terms.يُعْتَقُ: is to be freed or emancipated
key_terms.ٱلْإِمَامُ: the Imam, the authoritative guide who states the ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if Muslims mistakenly kill a believer living in enemy territory?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a Muslim who was residing among hostile non-Muslims and was mistakenly killed by Muslims. The Imam عليه السلام rules that a believing slave must be freed in expiation, citing the Qur'anic ruling for a believer from an enemy people.
